Global Nourish Corp. - Q3 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Nourish Corp. Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Nourish Corp.'s Q3 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Growth Officer; and Morgan Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on eight key areas: key achievements and challenges in the quarter, capital expenditure plans and priorities, performance of key brands and product categories, gross margin analysis drivers and trends, volume and price/mix analysis, impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions, overall company performance highlights, and revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance.

First, regarding key achievements and challenges in the quarter: As a leading player in the food and beverage industry, spanning convenient snacks, functional beverages, and plant-based dairy alternatives, we delivered a resilient quarter amid a dynamic macroeconomic backdrop. Consolidated net sales reached $2.82 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year, or 5.8% organically excluding FX and acquisitions. This marks our third straight quarter of accelerating organic growth, outpacing the industry's 3-4% global CAGR per NielsenIQ. Volume grew 2.1 points from strong demand for health-focused SKUs, while pricing added 3.7 points amid easing inflation.

By segment, snacks and convenience, 52% of sales, rose 9.1% organically to $1.47 billion, with North American savory snacks market share up 110 basis points to 18.2% per IRI, driven by our NutriCrunch air-popped, high-protein chips gaining against Pringles and Lay's through 12% higher A&P spend to $180 million on clean-label messaging. Beverages, 28% of sales, grew 6.4% organically to $790 million, with VitaQuench low-sugar electrolytes up 15% in APAC via Alibaba and Shopee partnerships, and kombucha up 22% in EMEA on premium trends. Plant-based and dairy alternatives, 20% of sales, increased 4.8% organically to $560 million, led by GreenMoo oat milk hitting 25% distribution in Mexico's top retailers in 90 days.

Operationally, we captured $145 million in gross margin gains, lifting adjusted margins to 38.4%, up 210 basis points, via Supply Chain Resilience 2.0, including AI demand forecasting with SAP S/4HANA across 15 plants, cutting inventory days 18% to 42, and Bayer partnerships reducing Brazilian cocoa costs 11%. Regionally, North America grew 8.5% organically with Costco gains, EMEA 6.2% despite UK inflation thanks to 40% recyclable packaging, APAC 12% on China's snacking boom, and LATAM 4.1% via local sourcing against Argentina FX issues.

Innovation drove 14 new SKUs, 70% health-aligned like low-sugar and vegan, contributing 22% of sales growth, with $95 million R&D including a Vietnam co-packing site for teas targeting ASEAN like Honest Tea.

Challenges included commodity inflation with wheat up 14% and sugar 9% per Bloomberg, pressuring COGS 180 basis points pre-hedges, though 85% coverage helped; unhedged palm oil added $22 million from Indonesian weather. Legacy carbonated drinks fell 3% in North America on functional shifts, prompting delisting 120 SKUs from our 2,500 portfolio. EMEA supply delays from Red Sea hiked freight 22%, FX shaved 1.4% growth, EU deforestation rules spurred $50 million RSPO pivot, and U.S. SNAP cuts loom for Q4 low-income volume.

Adjusted operating income rose 10% to $420 million, EPS $1.12 beating consensus by $0.04, with SG&A at 22.1% and FCF $320 million funding $150 million repurchases. This reinforces our Nourish Forward strategy: premium health portfolios to 65% of sales by 2026, net-zero Scope 1/2 by 2035, blockchain cocoa traceability, and $300 million capex for aseptic lines chasing RTD coffee.

Second, concerning capital expenditure plans and priorities: We're guiding FY2025 capex to $2.8 billion, or 4.2% of projected sales, up 12% from $2.5 billion last year, balancing growth and efficiency for ROIC above 12-15%, supporting 5-7% organic CAGR to 2029. Capacity expansion takes $1.2 billion or 43%, with $450 million for U.S. greenfields in tortilla/veggie chips and protein bars adding 25% savory capacity by 2026 at 22%+ EBITDA margins. APAC gets $350 million including $200 million Guangdong beverage plant for teas/electrolytes mirroring Coke gains, LATAM $150 million for Yerba Mate/coconut water on 18% functional growth per Euromonitor.

Digital/automation is $900 million or 32%, with $400 million Industry 4.0 AI demand sensing like Blue Yonder and IoT maintenance boosting OEE 15% to 94% in pilots; $300 million robotics for depalletizing in UK biscuits cutting costs 20%; $200 million automated DCs in U.S. Southwest, Mexico, SEA for e-com surge. Sustainability retrofits $700 million or 25%, $300 million regenerative irrigation with Indigo Ag saving 25% water on almonds/oats; $250 million biomass/heat pumps like Nestlé at 18% IRR.

Allocation: North America 45% ($1.26B), EMEA 25% ($700M), APAC 20% ($560M), LATAM 10% ($280M), average payback 2.8 years, 85% NPV-positive at 15%+ WACC. Funds 70% operations, net debt/EBITDA 2.1x, de-risking via 30% less external dependency, positioning for health (35% sales), ESG gains, premium mix +4.2%. FY2026 $3.0-3.2B, flex 10-15% if macros weaken, enabling 10%+ EPS CAGR, $15B FCF to 2029.

Third, in terms of performance of key brands and product categories: Our diversified lineup across snacks, beverages, dairy/plant-based, and convenience, with 12 brands at 85% revenues, drove 9.2% organic growth for core brands, beating industry 4.5% per NielsenIQ, from 5.1% volume, 3.8% pricing, 0.3% mix to premiums.

Snacks led at 14.3% organic, 28% revenue; CrunchMax up 11% volumes on AirFried low-oil crisps gaining 2.2 share points in U.S. savory per IRI via FlashRoast tech; NutriBite +22% with 15,000 C-store doors, +6.2% pricing no velocity loss. North America 65% growth, APAC 28% e-com to 18%, Europe +4% with UK multipack share. SKU exits 12%, focus 20 innovations for $25B better-for-you market at 7% CAGR.

Beverages 6.8% organic, 35% portfolio; SparkVita +18% on CollagenBoost gaining 320 bps U.S. RTD share, 4.1% Mexico; FizzCore flat volume +5% pricing with SweetSwap stevia vs. regs. North America +7%, APAC +12% China premium, EMEA -2% offset by zero-sugar +25%. AI forecasting cut stockouts 22%, $50M aseptic for shelf life.

Dairy/plant-based 11.5% organic, 22% revenues; PlantPure +26% on OatGlow in 40% Starbucks/Dunkin'; VitaCream +7%. North America +13%, Europe +10% +400 bps share, APAC +8%. $120M regen ag on 30% oats by FY25, water -25%, Gen Z favorability +15%.

Convenience 4.2% organic, 15%; QuickMeal +9% Walmart/Kroger distro; FreshBurst flat but mix +2. North America +6%, APAC +7%, Europe -1% offset robotic gains.

Premium/health 42% sales +250 bps EBITDA to 22.1%; e-com 14% +300 bps; NexGen cut logistics 8%, delivery 98%. Pillars: 10 Q4 launches for 15% 2025 sales, $200M Brazil plant-based M&A, pricing tiers vs. private label.

Fourth, looking at gross margin analysis: drivers and trends: We achieved 42.5% consolidated gross margin for full year 2023, up 230 bps from 40.2%, third year expansion at 180 bps CAGR; adjusted 43.1% ex-FX/disruptions.

Mix shift +120 bps: premiums/health like Organic Harvest bars/PlantPure at mid-50% vs. 35% legacy, 28% revenue +18% growth, SKU prune 15%. Pricing +100 bps: 6.2% average, 7.5% NA bevs, 5-8% snacks no elasticity hit, +50 bps U.S. salty share. COGS mitigation +80 bps net: inputs +4.1% (cocoa +22%, dairy +8%, wheat +6%), but 75% cocoa hedge at $3,200/MT vs. $4,100 spot; PET light 12% save $45M; yields +2.2% AI maintenance waste to 3.4%; freight -9% nearshoring Mexico.

Trends: Q4'21 39.8%, FY'22 40.2%, FY'23 42.5%, +270 bps 36 months vs. S&P F&B 110 bps. NA 44.8% +310 bps pricing/mix; EMEA 39.2% +50 bps energy/reg offset; APAC/LATAM 41.1% +210 bps local hedge.

Initiatives: SAP S/4 80% plants forecast +15%; 65% Rainforest cocoa +5% yields; $150M U.S. dairy integration +200 bps by 2026; monk fruit cuts sweeteners 18%. 2024 guide 43.0-43.8% +50-130 bps.

Fifth, reviewing volume and price/mix analysis: Organic net revenue +5.2% to $18.7B reported +4.1% ex-1.8% FX/0.4% divest. Price/mix +6.3% offset volume -1.1%, passing sugar/cocoa/Al +8-10%, premium shift.

Beverages 62% +4.8%: volume -1.5% away-home soft, at-home e-com 12%; price/mix +6.3% 5-7% CSDs like Refresh Cola, mix +1.1% zero-sugar 28%, functionals +15% $12B RTD.

Snacks/Nutrition 38% +5.9%: volume +0.4% protein NutriCrunch +12% +1.2 share vs. Ritz/Pringles; price/mix +5.5% ASP +6.8% elasticity -0.4.

NA 52% +4.1% volume flat, CSD -2% offset juices +8%, price/mix +7.2% club velocity +3%; EMEA 22% +6.8% volume +2.1% distro, price/mix +4.7% HFSS shift; LATAM 15% +9.2% volume +3.4% street trade; APAC 11% +1.5% volume -2.2% offset India +5%.

Health Forward $500M R&D 50 low-sugar SKUs 35% mix FY26; AI RGM +120 bps mix; recycled PET +2-3% premium. Q3 guide 4-6% price/mix +5-7% volumes flat.

Sixth, analyzing impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions: COGS +18% organic, commodities +28%: corn/wheat +35% Ukraine/drought $45M snacks; sugar +25% $0.18-0.23 PureSpring; cocoa +42% disease/El Niño; dairy +16% avian flu. Packaging Al +15%, corrugate +12%; freight +30% Red Sea palm oil 4-6 wk delay; labor +11%. Margins -320 bps to 31.8%, EBITDA -150 bps to 14.2%.

NA 55% rev +20% trucking/port; EMEA +24% energy; APAC +14% localized. Mitigated: pricing 12% waves 85% snacks pass-through ASP +9%; delist 15% SKUs $20M WC; hedge 65% corn $5.80 vs $7.20, 75% FY25; diversify palm 30% RSPO Malaysia/Colombia; 5k acre U.S. farm 10% self-suff 2026 +15% yields; AI SAP 92% forecast -18% stock $30M save; blockchain 60% chain disputes 5 days; drones John Deere.

Premiums favor: HarvestCrunch 25% sales +22% pricing; plant-based hedge nut +8% vs dairy; private label 12%. Q4 inflation 8-10% margins 33%+ pricing 5-7% volume +2%. EBITDA +5% $320M resilient.

Seventh, examining overall company performance highlights: Net revenues $15.8B +9% reported/6% organic, eighth quarter growth > industry 3-4%; FY organic raised 5-7%. Adj EBITDA $3.2B +12% margins +180 bps 20.3%; gross 45.1% +220 bps hedges 85% 2024; EPS $1.62 +14% beat 5c.

Volume +2% pricing balance, premium shift +1.2 snack share vs Frito/Mondelēz. Beverages 42% +11% $6.6B AquaPure low-sugar + hydration 18%; Snacks 35% +7% $5.5B NutriBoost +25%; Dairy 23% flat PlantPure +22%.

NA 48% +10% volume +3% e-com 18%; EMEA 25% +8% rPET 65%; APAC 20% +12% RTD teas +15%; LATAM 7% +5% coffee pods +20%.

FlavorChain 2.0 forecast -25% inventory 65 days $150M freight save; regen 35% Scope 3 -15%; R&D $450M 20% success fermented snacks. $2.2B BioNutri acq, divest $500M; Project Lean $800M savings +200 bps. Raise FY: 6-8% organic, 20.5% EBITDA, $6.55-6.65 EPS.

Eighth, considering revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance: Reaffirming FY guidance: net rev $15.8-16.3B 4-6% organic; core EPS $4.75-4.95 +150 bps margins; EBITDA margins 18.5-19.0% +100-150 bps; FCF $2.1-2.3B for $1.2B repurchases, dividend growth.

Tailwinds: NA volumes +4.1% PureVital +28% share vs Coke/Pepsi; premium 42% mix. NA 6-7% e-com 15%; APAC 11% teas/snacks; Europe mid-single H2 inflation ease. Costs peak hedged 85% $250M savings; ZBB $400M footprint gross 42.5% +180 bps SG&A -50 bps.

12 Q3-Q4 launches GreenLeaf shakes; recyc Al 70%. No major risks, FX hedged 60/40, 80% domestic sourcing. High-end EPS potential Health acceleration.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Lee (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3. Net sales were $2.82 billion, representing a 7.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.4%, impacted by moderating commodity inflation offset by pricing and efficiencies. Operating income was $420 million, and earnings per share were $1.12. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for 5-7% organic sales growth, adjusted EPS of $4.75 to $4.95, and EBITDA margin expansion of 100 to 150 basis points.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Doe (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thanks, John. Inflation has been a key headwind, with COGS up 18% organically from 28% commodity spikes like corn/wheat +35%, sugar +25%, cocoa +42%, and dairy +16% avian flu. Packaging and freight added layers with Al +15%, Red Sea +30%. This compressed gross margins 320 bps to 31.8%, but we've countered with 12% pricing waves achieving 85-70% pass-through, hedges covering 65-75% needs, palm diversification, and AI forecasting saving $30 million. Premiums and SKU rationalization insulated us, keeping EBITDA up 5%. We expect moderation to 8-10% Q4 as harvests normalize.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Smith with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Jane Smith (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for VitaQuench and what is the expected impact of the product?

Taylor Kim (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Jane. VitaQuench, our low-sugar electrolyte line, drove 15% volume uplift in APAC through e-com with Alibaba/Shopee, capturing share from Monster/Red Bull. Plans include $200 million Guangdong plant expansion for RTD formats, targeting 20%+ share like Coke peers. Expect 18% overall growth contribution, lifting beverages to 6-7% organic with 320 bps U.S./Mexico share gains via innovations like CollagenBoost, pushing premium mix to 42% and adding 250 bps to EBITDA margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Mike Johnson (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Morgan Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, Mike. Disruptions like Red Sea delays hiked freight 22-30%, EMEA palm oil leads +4-6 weeks, and avian flu/port congestion persist. We're countering with Supply Chain Resilience 2.0: AI SAP/Blue Yonder forecast to 92% accuracy -18% stock, blockchain IBM 60% traceability disputes to 5 days, drone monitoring, 30% palm shift RSPO Malaysia/Colombia, 5k acre U.S. farms for 10% self-sufficiency +15% yields. NexGen cut logistics 8%, delivery 98%, inventory 42-65 days. Capex $900M automation adds resilience, positioning for 2% volume growth.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Jordan Lee (CFO):
Thanks, Emily. Q4 organic sales 5-7%, EPS $1.15-1.20, margins 38-39% on holiday tailwinds/inflation ease. FY reaffirmed at 4-6% organic revenue, EPS $4.75-4.95 high-end potential, EBITDA +100-150 bps. Tailwinds from premium 42% mix, e-com 15%, hedged costs $250M savings, 12 launches. Risks like FX/tariffs mitigated by 60/40 hedges/80% domestic. Confident in 10-12% EPS growth FY25 as efficiencies scale.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in Global Nourish Corp. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
